mcq.QUESTION_DESC:
Consider the following code:

sq.ANSWER: The synchronized keyword ensures mutual exclusion by allowing only one thread to access a block/method at a time. It prevents data inconsistency in concurrent environments.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: What is the role of synchronized keyword in Java thread management?

sq.ANSWER:
• One thread calls wait() and releases the lock.

  • Another thread (holding the same lock) calls notify() or notifyAll() to wake the waiting thread(s).

  • Ensures coordination between threads, especially in producer-consumer scenarios.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: How does inter-thread communication occur using wait(), notify(), and notifyAll()?

lq.ANSWER:
class Account {
    private int balance = 1000;

    public synchronized void withdraw(int amount) {
        while (balance < amount) {
            System.out.println("Insufficient balance. Waiting...");
            try {
                wait();
            } catch (InterruptedException e) {}
        }
        balance -= amount;
        System.out.println("Withdrawn: " + amount + ", Remaining: " + balance);
    }

    public synchronized void deposit(int amount) {
        balance += amount;
        System.out.println("Deposited: " + amount + ", New Balance: " + balance);
        notifyAll();
    }
}

public class BankApp {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Account acc = new Account();

        Thread t1 = new Thread(() -> acc.withdraw(1200));
        Thread t2 = new Thread(() -> acc.deposit(500));

        t1.start();
        t2.start();
    }
}
